assumptions: A slot is an authored scheduling opportunity, with no physical duration or RF modulation assigned.
The transmitter can offer one frame on each ideal independent channel simultaneously; receiver radio count alone does not increase transmitted capacity.
Each independently tuned radio collects at most one channel frame per modeled slot; four radios can cover four channels.
Receivers already know the channel plan, manifest cadence and common slot clock; partial receivers prefer the anchor channel on predicted manifest slots.
T=128, N=1, Al=4; full single-symbol RFC6330 packets are wrapped in authored authenticated frames.
Manifest repeats, signatures and framing consume the recorded slot and wire-byte budget.
The repair floor reserves channel opportunities for round-robin retained generations; zero is an exploratory counterfactual.
Catch-up depends on retention, receive opportunities, offered work and actual decoder success; it is not guaranteed by fountain coding alone.

observations.interpretation: Catch-up is conditional on this finite production tail, retention window and modeled receive opportunities. Completion uses actual RaptorQ reconstruction.
